# skeleton-nodejs-tsoa-tsyringe

Minimal, production-shaped **Node.js + TypeScript** backend skeleton built around
**Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**, **TSOA** (decorator-based controllers + auto-generated
OpenAPI/routes) and **TSyringe** (dependency injection), with **MongoDB/Mongoose** and **Vitest**.

It ships with two bounded contexts as references:

- `health` — trivial controller-only context (`GET /health/status`).
- `item` — full **Controller → Service → Repository → Mongo** example (CRUD).

---

## Stack

| Concern | Tool |
|--------|------|
| Language / Runtime | TypeScript + Node.js |
| HTTP framework | Express |
| Controllers + OpenAPI | TSOA |
| Dependency Injection | TSyringe (`reflect-metadata`) |
| Database | MongoDB + Mongoose |
| Logging | Winston (via `ILogger`) |
| Auth (JWT helper) | `jsonwebtoken` |
| Testing | Vitest + `mongodb-memory-server` + supertest |
| Lint / Format | ESLint + Prettier (Husky pre-commit) |

---

## Architecture

Every bounded context in `src/contexts/<name>/` follows the same 4 layers, with dependencies
always pointing **inward**:

```
contexts/<name>/
├── domain/           # Pure business types. NO framework imports.
│   ├── entities/         # Entities / interfaces
│   └── repositories/     # Repository INTERFACES + Symbol.for() tokens
├── application/      # Business logic / orchestration. Depends on domain only.
│   └── services/
├── infrastructure/   # Framework implementations. Depends on domain + application.
│   ├── <Name>Module.ts   # DI registration for the context
│   └── persistence/      # Mongo models + repository implementations
└── entrypoint/       # TSOA controllers (HTTP). Depends on all the above.
```

### The core pattern: Controller → Service → Repository

```
HTTP request
  → Controller (entrypoint)   thin: extract input, delegate, return
    → Service (application)   ALL business logic
      → Repository interface  (domain) — bound to a Mongo impl in infrastructure
        → MongoDB
```

Rules of thumb:

- **Controllers are thin** — no business logic, no direct DB access.
- **Services own the logic** and depend on repository **interfaces** (injected by token).
- **Repositories** are the only place that touches Mongoose, and they return **plain
  domain objects** (`.lean()`), never Mongoose documents.
- **Never `new` a service** — register it in the context module and `@inject` it.
- **Never use `console.*`** — inject `ILogger`.

See `src/contexts/item/` for the canonical implementation.

## Project layout

```
src/
├── infrastructure/
│   ├── start.ts              # entrypoint: loads .env, boots Skeleton
│   ├── Skeleton.ts           # connects Mongo (optional) + starts Server
│   ├── server.ts             # Express app: middleware, routes, swagger
│   ├── env/                  # config.ts (serverConfig + JWT_SECRET), environment.ts
│   ├── ioc/
│   │   ├── container.ts          # registers every context module (infra first)
│   │   ├── InfrastructureModule.ts  # ILogger, HttpClient
│   │   ├── Type.ts               # DI tokens (Symbol.for)
│   │   ├── moduleContainerBase.ts
│   │   └── logger/Logger.ts      # Winston ILogger
│   ├── middlewares/          # auth, correlationId, error handler
│   ├── MongoDB/              # connectMongo()
│   └── routes/               # AUTO-GENERATED by TSOA (do not edit)
├── contexts/
│   ├── health/
│   └── item/                 # DDD reference context
├── shared/                   # cross-cutting domain (errors, value objects, helpers)
└── tests/                    # Vitest specs
```

---

## Getting started

```bash
# 1. Install deps
npm install

# 2. Create your local env (all values are optional for a first boot)
cp .env.example .env.local

# 3. Run in watch mode (regenerates TSOA routes + restarts on change)
npm run dev
```

The server starts on `http://localhost:8080`:

- Health check: `GET http://localhost:8080/health/status`
- Items CRUD:   `GET/POST http://localhost:8080/items`
- Swagger UI:   `http://localhost:8080/api-docs`

> **MongoDB is optional.** If `MONGO_URI` is empty the app boots without a database
> (the `item` endpoints will fail at query time until you set a URI). Set `MONGO_URI`
> in `.env.local` to enable persistence.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `NODE_ENV` | `local` | Selects which `.env.<NODE_ENV>` file is loaded |
| `MONGO_URI` | _(empty)_ | MongoDB connection string. Empty = boot without DB |
| `JWT_SECRET` | `MISSING_SECRET` | Secret used by the JWT helper / auth middleware |

---

## Scripts

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `npm run dev` | Watch mode (nodemon + ts-node) with live TSOA route regen |
| `npm run build` | `tsoa spec-and-routes` → `tsc` → copy env to `dist` |
| `npm start` | Run the compiled app from `dist` |
| `npm run tsoa:routes` | Regenerate `src/infrastructure/routes` (OpenAPI + routes) |
| `npm test` | Run the Vitest suite once |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode |
| `npm run test:coverage` | Vitest with coverage report |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint with autofix |

## How to add a new bounded context

1. Create the folders:

   ```
   src/contexts/<name>/
   ├── domain/entities/<Name>.ts
   ├── domain/repositories/I<Name>Repository.ts   # interface + Symbol.for() token
   ├── application/services/<Name>Service.ts
   ├── infrastructure/<Name>Module.ts
   ├── infrastructure/persistence/<Name>Model.ts
   ├── infrastructure/persistence/Mongo<Name>Repository.ts
   └── entrypoint/<Name>Controller.ts
   ```

2. In `<Name>Module.ts`, bind the repository token to its Mongo implementation and
   register the service:

   ```ts
   container.register(<NAME>_REPOSITORY, { useClass: Mongo<Name>Repository })
   container.registerSingleton(<Name>Service)
   ```

3. Register the module in `src/infrastructure/ioc/container.ts`
   (keep `InfrastructureModule` first).

4. Regenerate routes: `npm run tsoa:routes`.

> Copy the `item` context as your template — it already wires all 4 layers correctly.

---

## Testing

Tests live in `src/tests/` and run with Vitest.

- **Service/repository tests** instantiate the real classes against an in-memory MongoDB
  (`mongodb-memory-server`) — see `src/tests/scenarios/item.test.ts`.
- **HTTP tests** hit the Express app with supertest — see `health.test.ts`.

```bash
npm test
```
